proposed_changes.after: Adams Township (Butler County) Board of Supervisors Resolution 2026-09, identified in the July 13, 2026 minutes as a curative amendment regarding data centers, power generation plant/systems, solar power systems, last-mile fulfillment center/micro-warehouses and dispensaries. A standalone executed resolution and its full operative text remain unverified.

proposed_changes.before: Butler Eagle reported a June 22, 2026 vote approving a 180-day application moratorium on six uses: data centers, power generation plants, large-scale and accessory solar systems, last-mile fulfillment centers, micro-warehouses, and dispensaries. It reported that the unanimous July 13 resolution followed the motion and allowed up to 180 days for a curative zoning amendment. Officials described the action as preemptive rather than responding to a pending application. The earlier review found no news of extension, amendment adoption or repeal through 2026-09-23; later action is not established by the retained sources. [VERIFY: operative start and end, final resolution text and subsequent action.]
proposed_changes.after: June 22 official minutes record a unanimous zoning-invalidity motion; July 13 official minutes record unanimous approval of Resolution 2026-09. The retained Butler Eagle accounts describe a 180-day moratorium and curative-amendment preparation period, but the minute entries do not reproduce a complete prohibition or establish the operative start, end or later force. [VERIFY: executed resolution, precise scope, interval and subsequent action.]

proposed_changes.before: Adams Township Board of Supervisors adopted a 180-day moratorium (via a June 22, 2026 motion, formalized by resolution on July 13, 2026) on six business types including data centers and large-scale solar, to allow time to draft a curative amendment to the zoning ordinance.
